Article Title: Behind the lights and grandeur: What it takes and costs to build a Durga Pujo pandal
Article Text:
​Before the dhak begins: The money and machinery behind a Durga pujo​

The quiet work before the dhak

The budget

The idol costs a fifth

A theme, decided half a year early

Six months, one theme, lakhs of rupees

Where the money comes from

What it costs to raise a Durga Pujo

What the numbers leave out

Long before the first beat of the dhak, a Durga Pujo has already been decided, priced and partly built. The goddess arrives in autumn, but the people who bring her to a neighbourhood start months earlier, with a theme, a budget and a list of permissions that must be collected one office at a time.To the crowds who walk through a pandal's gates, a pujo is a few days of colour, light and sound. To the club that puts it up, it is a yearly project that runs on money raised from the neighbourhood, a small circle of skilled craftsmen and a large number of people who all have to be in the right place on the right day. In West Bengal that project is repeated in locality after locality, each with its own ledger.The ledger is not small. A medium-scale pujo costs several lakh rupees, and the biggest share does not go to the idol at the centre of it all. It goes to the structure built around her. Most visitors never see the figures, the deadlines or the people behind them, and that is exactly how the organisers want it. A pujo is meant to arrive as a finished thing.Nirmal, a pujo organiser from West Bengal who has run one for the past 10 years, knows that ledger well. "A medium scale pujo in West Bengal would cost somewhere between 10 to 15 lakhs," he says. "Every year the budget increases as per the market inflation."That second sentence matters as much as the first. A committee that spent a certain amount last year should expect to spend more this year on the same pujo, before it adds a single new ambition. For a club working with money collected from its neighbours, the target keeps moving upward, and the neighbours are asked to keep up with it.Ask him what costs the most and the answer is immediate. "The pandal costs the most," he says. Not the lighting, not the idol, not the food. He puts the pandal at around Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh for a medium-scale pujo, which makes it the line the rest of the budget has to work around.Next to the pandal, the idol is a modest line. "Whatever the pandal costs, the idol costs its one-fifth," Nirmal says. For a medium-scale pujo, that works out to around Rs 80,000.It is a striking ratio. The figure at the heart of the festival, the one every visitor has come to see, costs a fraction of the structure that shelters her.Within the idol's cost, the most expensive element is gold. Certain gold items are designated for it, among them an ornament that is given by the club organising the pujo. The ornament comes from the organisers themselves, which makes it a different kind of expense from the rest.A pandal needs a theme, and the theme needs time. "The theme is decided at least six months ago," Nirmal says, meaning at least six months before the pujo. That is a long lead for a festival that lasts only days.Who decides it varies. In some committees, he says, there is a specific person whose sole job is deciding the theme. In others, the pandal makers can decide it too. The choice matters for more than looks, because the budget is also decided through the theme. Once the idea is fixed, the cost of building it can be worked out, and the money follows.This is why the calendar starts so early. A theme chosen six months out leaves room to price the work, find the right artisan and settle the budget before construction begins. By the time the neighbourhood sees the first bamboo go up, the important decisions have already been made.Construction is where the calendar turns uncertain. Asked how long a medium-scale pandal takes to build, Nirmal is candid. "It depends on the workers, to be honest," he says. "Some can build the same pandal in two months, whereas some will require more time."The reason, as he describes it, is a shortage of skill. "The skilled pandal makers are not a lot in number. Mostly there is just one skilled artisan and a lot of people work under him."That structure explains a good deal. The quality of the pandal and the speed at which it rises rest heavily on one person, with a large crew following his lead. For an organiser, choosing a pandal maker is therefore as much a scheduling decision as a financial one. A maker who is slow, or one who is booked elsewhere, can put the whole timeline at risk.The funding model is local. "Every area or colony has a designated club which builds a pandal," Nirmal explains. "And then they get chanda, donations, advertisements that ultimately make the pujo what it is."There is also help from the state. This year, he says, the West Bengal government is providing Rs 1 lakh to small-scale pujos, and electricity is completely free. Free power removes a bill that would otherwise sit beside the lighting and the pandal. The Rs 1 lakh grant, though, is meant for small-scale pujos. Set against a medium-scale budget of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh, most of the money still has to come from the neighbourhood, from donors and from advertisers.Some costs are smaller but just as fixed. The priest's expenditure, Nirmal says, is around Rs 30,000 to Rs 40,000. The dhaki, whose drumming is as much a part of the pujo as the idol, is paid around Rs 10,000. On top of that, he gets free food, lodging and clothes.Those extras are part of the arrangement. A dhaki who is housed and fed for the duration of the pujo is a cost the committee carries beyond the headline fee. Nirmal was also asked about bhog expenditure, but his answer covered only the priest and the dhaki.Add up the lines Nirmal named, the pandal, the idol, the priest and the dhaki, and the total lands somewhere between roughly Rs 4.2 lakh and Rs 6.3 lakh. His estimate for the whole pujo is Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh.The gap is considerable. It covers everything else a pujo needs, including the lighting and food he named only to rule them out as the biggest expense. Nirmal did not break down how that money is divided.Asked about the biggest challenge organisers face, Nirmal does not name a single expense. "The biggest challenge is that everything from the beginning to the end is completed properly," he says.That includes permissions. "You have to get proper permissions like the police and the fire department," he says, "and it takes a lot of people to complete a pujo and to make a pujo what it is."The pandal maker and his crew, the artisan working on the idol, the priest, the dhaki and the club members collecting funds are all working towards the same date. Seen this way, the Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh is only part of what a pujo demands. The rest is coordination, and much of Nirmal's decade in the job has gone into it.For the people who walk through the gates, the pujo arrives as a finished thing. For the club behind it, it began at least six months earlier with a decision about a theme, and it will begin again next year at a higher cost.

Article Title: First the ancestors, then the Gods
Article Text:
Dia de los Muertos

Obon

Thirukkural

Thenpulathaar Deivam Virundhokkal Thaanendraangu

Iympulathaaru Ombal Thalai

Mahalaya Amavasya has just passed, ending a sacred period of remembrance for our ancestors . As the anticipation of Navarathri fills the air, we move from honouring those who came before us to celebrating the divine feminine. Yet, between these observances lies a profound connection: our lives are rooted in the past, even as we journey towards the future.Across civilizations, humanity has found ways to honour the departed. In Chinese shrines, three incense sticks are offered, symbolising ancestors, the present generation and future descendants. In Mexico,, the Day of the Dead, celebrates the departed with food and flowers. In Japan,is observed with the belief that ancestral spirits return to visit their families. Rituals differ, but the sentiment remains universal: love does not end with death.In Hindu tradition , performing ancestral rites is regarded not simply as a choice, but as a sacred duty.Water occupies a place of profound significance in these rituals. Water is more than a natural element. It purifies, heals and connects the physical with the spiritual. Offering water to ancestors expresses gratitude and invokes their peace. Even in grief, flowing river offers comfort through its symbolism of transition, surrender and liberation. Fire purifies the physical; water, in its sacred symbolism, becomes a medium of spiritual release.An intriguing historical anecdote brings this tradition into focus. After Aurangzeb confined his father, Shah Jahan, in the Agra Fort in 1658, the ageing emperor lived under strict restrictions. Shah Jahan reproached his son for denying him adequate water, observing the irony that Hindus offered water and reverence even to departed ancestors, while his own son denied these to a living father. The poignancy of this remark endures: if reverence is owed to those beyond our sight, how much greater should our compassion be towards those still beside us?Thiruvalluvar, too, places ancestral obligations at the very beginning of the householder's duties. In43, he writes:The householder's foremost duties are towards the departed, the divine, guests, relatives and oneselfWhy does the poet place the departed before even the gods ? Perhaps he recognises that gratitude begins by acknowledging those whose lives and sacrifices have shaped our own.We do not know Valluvar 's religious identity. Yet his reference to ancestral duties suggests that honouring the departed was deeply embedded in the cultural life of his time.Across traditions, food, water and other offerings are made in memory of the dead, often through acts of charity. Perhaps what we offer to those we can see finds its way, through mysterious cosmic pathways, to those we cannot.An ancient prayer- Pithru Gayathri Manthra - expresses this enduring hope: Let us meditate upon the ancestors, the sustainers of the world; may they guide our consciousness.The departed may no longer walk beside us, but their footsteps remain on our paths. May their blessings dissolve our obstacles and strengthen our resolve.We are each a living chapter in a story written by generations before us, entrusted with the beautiful responsibility of being the link that carries their legacy into generations yet to come.
Article Summary: Navarathri has just passed, ending a sacred period of remembrance for our ancestors. Across civilizations, humanity has found ways to honour the departed. Rituals differ, but the sentiment remains universal: love does not end with death. Offering water to ancestors expresses gratitude and invokes their peace.

Article Title: Kharge writes to PM Modi: Call all-party meet on delimitation bill
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Amid speculation of govt planning a special session of Parliament to pass delimitation bill, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge Friday wrote to PM Narendra Modi , urging him to convene an all-party meeting to discuss Constitution Amendment bill. He said any far-reaching legislation on important issues, such as delimitation, must be discussed before being brought to Parliament.Alluding to the possibility of a special session, Kharge noted that 64 days have passed since Parliament's monsoon session was adjourned sine die on Aug 13, but Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha have not been prorogued yet. He called it an "unprecedented scenario".Kharge underlined to PM that this is his fourth request for an all-party meeting. He said the first plea came on April 11, which went unheeded, and govt brought the delimitation bill in Parliament on April 16. He said the bill failed to muster two-third majority by a decisive margin. Kharge noted that he wrote to the PM for all-party meetings again on July 16 and Aug 27."Please convene an all-party meeting to have a detailed discussion on your new proposals before they are finalised for consideration in Parliament. All l parties must get sufficient time to deliberate among themselves, with each other and with all other stakeholders. Please do not once again try and bulldoze a far-reaching Constitutional Amendment Bill through Parliament as you attempted earlier and that met its well-deserved fate," he said.

He said the first plea came on April 11, which went unheeded, and govt brought the delimitation bill in Parliament on April 16. Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

-

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: Ryan Clark challenges Stephen A. Smith over Lane Johnson’s retirement as Eagles star puts mental health first
Article Text:
Ryan Clark challenges Stephen A. Smith over Lane Johnson’s retirement as Eagles star puts mental health first

The Pivot Podcast

Ryan Clark tells Stephen A. Smith why Lane Johnson’s mental health matters

The Pivot Podcast

First Take

Lane Johnson explains his retirement as Ryan Clark defends his decision

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ryan Clark has defended Lane Johnson after Stephen A. Smith questioned the Philadelphia Eagles tackle’s decision to retire during the 2026 NFL season. Speaking on, Clark said that a person’s intentions matter less than the effect their words have on others. He also praised Johnson for putting his mental health and family first, while pointing out why Smith’s comments deserved criticism despite his later apology.Clark made his position clear while discussing Johnson’s retirement and the reaction to it. He said he was proud of the veteran offensive tackle for choosing what was best for him rather than forcing himself to continue playing football.“Lane Johnson’s football career has been about intent and impact. And I think more people should understand that,” Clark said on. He also welcomed Smith’s apology but stressed that good intentions do not erase the effect a person’s words can have.“Your intent doesn’t matter. It’s about your impact. It’s about what people see in you, how you’ve changed people’s lives,” Clark added.His comments came after Smith faced criticism for the way he discussed Johnson’s decision on ESPN’s. On October 7, one day after the retirement announcement, Smith questioned why Johnson had chosen to walk away when the Eagles were struggling through a difficult stretch of the season.The Eagles were 2-2 at the time and had suffered back-to-back losses. Smith also pointed to the team’s injury problems and the absence of key players, including A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith, while questioning Johnson’s timing.During the discussion, Smith repeatedly referred to Johnson’s mental health in a sarcastic tone. That approach drew criticism because Johnson had clearly explained that his emotional well-being and family priorities were behind his decision.Clark’s response focused on the difference between questioning a player’s timing and dismissing the personal reasons behind such a major life choice. For him, Johnson’s decision showed that looking after yourself can matter more than staying in a sport, even when your team still needs you.Johnson announced his retirement on October 6, bringing an end to a 14-season career with the Philadelphia Eagles. The veteran offensive lineman admitted that walking away was difficult, especially because he had hoped to play one more season alongside his teammates.“I deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year; to take the field with my brothers for one last season,” Johnson wrote in his retirement statement.However, he explained that his priorities had changed and that continuing to play was no longer the right choice for him.“Right now it is critical that I focus on my mental health. I owe it to my teammates, coaches, the organization and the fans to have my head and heart 100 percent in the game,” Johnson said. “And right now my heart is telling me that it’s time to say goodbye to football.”Johnson’s words made it clear that he did not want to continue playing unless he could give the game his full attention. He also wanted to put his family and personal well-being first rather than extend his career for another season.Clark praised that choice, noting that Johnson had previously spoken about protecting his mental health and was now following the same principle in his own life. His message was that stepping away does not make someone weak, even when that person is a physically strong and successful athlete.
Article Summary: Lane Johnson announced his retirement on October 6, bringing an end to a 14-season career with the Philadelphia Eagles. Stephen A. Smith questioned why Johnson had chosen to walk away when the Eagles were struggling through a difficult stretch of the season. Ryan Clark defended Johnson, saying that a person's intentions matter less than the effect their words have on others.

Former Sri Lanka all-rounder Chaminda Vaas is set for his maiden coaching stint in the Indian Premier League after being appointed Delhi Capitals' fast bowling coach ahead of the 2027 season.Vaas, one of Sri Lanka's most successful fast bowlers, claimed 355 wickets in Tests and 400 in ODIs during his international career. Article Title: 8 dead, 8 injured as mini bus plunges into 15-feet drain on Delhi-Mumbai Expressway near Kota
Article Text:
A bus overturned on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway in Kota





KOTA: At least eight persons were killed and eight others injured after a mini bus carrying around 23 members of a family from Madhya Pradesh veered off the road and fell into a 15-foot-deep drain along the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway under Simliya police station in Kota district early Saturday morning.The family members departed from Bhopal around 7 pm Friday and headed to Khatu Shyamji temple in Sikar district of Rajasthan. The accident took place around 6 am Saturday.Rescue operations were swiftly launched, though team efforts were severely hampered by mud and accumulated water inside the drain. Emergency personnel deployed cranes at the spot to lift the damaged vehicle and recover trapped individuals.Confirming the details of the ongoing operation, Simliya SHO Nand Singh told TOI that eight bodies have been retrieved from the wreckage so far. He noted that around 23 passengers were on board the traveller bus during the crash.The injured were rushed to nearby medical facilities, including New Medical College Hospital and MBS Hospital in Kota, with three ambulances deployed for quick transportation, the SHO said. Eight injured passengers have been admitted to the two medical facilities for treatment, police said.While official casualties currently stand at eight fatalities, authorities fear the death toll may rise as rescue teams continue to clear the site and verify victim identities.Identities of those killed and injured are yet to be ascertained, along with other details of the passengers, the SHO said.
Article Summary: A mini bus carrying around 23 members of a family from Madhya Pradesh veered off the road and fell into a 15-foot-deep drain along the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway. Article Title: Deva, composer whose music announced Rajinikanth's stardom, dies at 75 in Chennai
Article Text:
Deva, a celebrated figure in Tamil cinema, has passed away in Chennai after experiencing chest pain





CHENNAI: Deva, the music director whose "Superstar" title-card music has announced every Rajinikanth film since 1992, including the latest, Jailer 2, died in Chennai on Saturday. He was 75.He complained of chest pain on Saturday morning and was taken to Surya Hospital. He died despite efforts to resuscitate him, doctors said.The godfather of Gaana, Deva was a music director, lyricist and singer who took the street music of Chennai into mainstream cinema. He wrote and sang many of his own gaana numbers and was a rage through the 1990s. The songs he made popular are now sung even at international film events.At a time when Ilaiyaraaja dominated Tamil cinema and AR Rahman was ushering in a musical revolution, Deva carved out his own identity by speaking the language of the common man. Rather than competing with the two musical stalwarts, he built his reputation on simple, catchy tunes, familiar rhythms and colloquial expressions that resonated with audiences.Affectionately known as Thenisai Thendral, he became one of the most sought-after composers of the 1990s.For Rajinikanth, he created the vibe for the star's introductory songs, including those in Annamalai and Baashha. The Baashha theme became synonymous with Rajinikanth's screen persona, while Naan Autokaaran became an anthem for autorickshaw drivers in this part of the country.Deva also demonstrated his versatility through his association with Kamal Haasan, composing for films such as Avvai Shanmugi, which showcased a different musical sensibility from the larger-than-life hero themes he created for Rajinikanth.Born Devanesan Chokkalingam on Nov 20, 1950, in Mylapore, he came to film music after working in television and stage shows. His early musical exposure included classical training under Dhanraj, Western musical studies and stage performances. He worked at Doordarshan's Podhigai channel and composed songs for the farming programme Vayalum Vaazhvum. While his brothers, Sabesh and Murali, were also in the music business, his son, Srikanth Deva, is a composer too.Deva made his debut in 1989 with Manasukketha Maharaasaa. Prashanth's Vaikasi Porandhaachu in 1990 gave him his big break, establishing his ability to deliver accessible and emotionally engaging music.His other hits included Aasai, Kaadhal Kottai, Naerukku Ner, Vaali, Avvai Shanmugi, Kushi and Panchathanthiram. He worked in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam, and his scores run to more than 400 films.Despite his success, Deva remained known for his humility and appreciation of fellow musicians. He spoke admiringly of Ilaiyaraaja and Rahman and welcomed the work of younger composers, maintaining a reputation for simplicity both in his music and in his personal demeanour.Members of the film industry posted messages in memory of Deva.
Article Summary: Deva was a music director, lyricist and singer who took the street music of Chennai into mainstream cinema. He wrote and sang many of his own gaana numbers and was a rage through the 1990s. The songs he made popular are now sung even at international film events.

The 32-year-old has left her home only five times this year and can suffer severe crashes after even short conversations or basic activities.Dobbin, who competed for Great Britain at the Tokyo Olympics, has spoken publicly about her condition despite knowing the interview itself could worsen her health. She hopes her story will raise awareness of ME and help people understand the seriousness of an illness that has changed almost every part of her life.Beth Dobbin said even a simple trip to the doctor can leave her bedridden for months. She now only gets out of bed to eat and use the bathroom.“I’ve done little things like attend a blood test at the doctors and been in bed for months after. So doing this interview, chatting away for 30 minutes, that could have an impact on me in 2027. But I felt like it was really important to do that to get the message out”, she said per BBC.ME is a chronic condition that can cause severe fatigue, pain, sleep problems and difficulties with thinking and memory. For Dobbin, even bright lights, loud sounds or conversations can trigger a crash.These episodes can last for days or, in severe cases, months.She added, “It’s life-decimating like I can’t even put into words,” she says. “I feel like I’ve lost everything. I have still got my family, but I’ve lost my independence, my health, the ability to work, the ability to exercise.”Dobbin believes her illness began after she had Covid and glandular fever during the winter of 2021-22. At first, she noticed only small changes. She was sleeping more and her running times had dropped slightly.Her condition then became progressively worse. She competed at the World Championships, Commonwealth Games and European Championships in 2022, despite experiencing a range of symptoms.At the European Championships, Dobbin lost all feeling in her legs while in the starting blocks and false-started. She later described that period as her “year of hell”.After the championships, her health deteriorated further. She struggled to stand, slept for long periods and spent increasing amounts of time in bed.Several specialists eventually told her that she had ME.“I wish it was just fatigue, that would be a walk in the park,” she says. “It’s so much more than that. If I thought of fatigue in my top 20 symptoms it might just make the cut.”Instead, she says, it feels like her entire body “is shutting down; it feels like you are a few days from death”.Her family has also been deeply affected. Her father Jim and mother Jean have described their worry about her future, while her sister Faye will run the Yorkshire Marathon to raise money for ME Research UK.Dobbin remains hopeful that increased research into ME and long Covid will eventually lead to better treatment.
Article Summary: Beth Dobbin has been diagnosed with myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME) The 32-year- old now spends more than 22 hours a day in bed. ME is a chronic condition that can cause severe fatigue, pain, sleep problems and difficulties with thinking and memory.

Article Title: Mumbai under heatwave warning for third consecutive day
Article Text:
IMD issued a heatwave warning for Thursday





MUMBAI: The city was under a heatwave warning for the third consecutive day on Wednesday with a yellow alert issued by the IMD For Oct 14, the weather bureau has warned of hot and humid weather conditions in isolated areas as temperatures continue to remain elevated.Maximum temperature recorded on Wednesday by the IMD Santacruz observatory was 37.8 deg C, which was 4.1 deg C above normal, while the IMD Colaba observatory recorded 36.4 deg C, which was 3.2 deg C above normal.Mumbai has been placed under a heatwave warning for Oct 15, with Oct 16 forecast to witness hot and humid weather conditions. Meanwhile, light to moderate rain and thundershowers are expected for Oct 17-18 for Mumbai and Thane.Just a day ago, the city had recorded a maximum temperature of 38°C, making it the second-hottest Oct day in 11 years. Meanwhile, mercury had touched 38.2°C on Monday, the highest Oct maximum recorded in the city during the same period.IMD officials too agreed that a prolonged heatwave for early in the month of Oct wasn’t very common.“The anticyclone which led to the first heatwave warning on Oct 9 last week has shifted slightly northwards, but an easterly wave is influencing the region, with temperatures likely to touch 37.8°C on Thursday.This will mean seven consecutive days of temperatures above 37°C, which is unusually oppressive for Mumbai. While the city does experience spells of two to three days of high temperatures, a continuous stretch of six to seven days is not normal. An easterly wave is a weather system characterised by a trough that travels from east to west. It is a feature of this season and can interact with weather systems approaching from the west, triggering intense thunderstorms. Its role in prolonging the current hot spell is a factor that needs to be examined, particularly in the context of a strong El Niño year,” said an IMD official.According to Akshay Sunil, Vice President, WeatherEx Pvt Ltd, “The heat over Mumbai is part of a broader warm spell across western India. A high-pressure circulation and easterly to northeasterly winds are limiting the usual cooling sea breeze, while clear post-monsoon skies are allowing strong daytime heating. Humidity adds to the discomfort. Our extended outlook suggests that above-normal temperatures may continue through at least October 22, although local light showers could bring temporary relief post Oct 22 in parts of Konkan. ”
Article Summary: Mumbai has been placed under a heatwave warning for Oct 15, with Oct 16 forecast to witness hot and humid weather conditions. Light to moderate rain and thundershowers are expected for Oct 17-18 for Mumbai and Thane. Maximum temperature recorded on Wednesday by the IMD Santacruz observatory was 37.8 deg C, 4.1 deg C above normal.

Article Title: Jaipur Murder: A poll contest, a family clash, 2 murders: How man killed his only son, daughter-in-law
Article Text:
The accused, identified as Ramchandra Jat, has been taken into custody, and an investigation is underway.

Dispute over sarpanch election

Couple run over while returning home

Voting scheduled for November 16





JAIPUR: A 60-year-old man allegedly ran over his only son and daughter-in-law with an SUV in Rajasthan’s Churu district after a dispute over his decision to contest the upcoming panchayat elections , police said.The incident took place late Tuesday night in Changoi village, under Taranagar tehsil. The accused, identified as Ramchandra Jat, has been taken into custody, and an investigation is underway.Taranagar police station head constable Suresh Kumar said Ramchandra operates a weighbridge in the village and wanted to contest the sarpanch election from Changoi.His 40-year-old son, Ravindra, and 35-year-old daughter-in-law, Mahindra, were allegedly opposed to his decision. This had led to frequent clashes between them over the past few days, police said.Another argument broke out at their home on Tuesday night. Ramchandra and Ravindra subsequently went to the weighbridge, and Mahindra joined them there after some time. The dispute over contesting the election allegedly continued at the site.Police said Ravindra and Mahindra were returning home when Ramchandra allegedly approached them from behind in his Bolero jeep and hit them, running them over.Locals rushed to the spot after hearing screams and alerted the police. The couple was taken to a government hospital in Taranagar, where their bodies were placed in the mortuary.Ravindra ran an e-Mitra shop in the village, while Mahindra was a homemaker. The couple is survived by their 11-year-old daughter.The incident comes ahead of the panchayat elections in Taranagar, where voting for the posts of panch and sarpanch is scheduled for November 16 as part of the fourth phase of the ongoing elections.Changoi was recently declared a new gram panchayat. Ramchandra reportedly became determined to contest the sarpanch election after the change.Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.
Article Summary: The incident took place late Tuesday night in Changoi village, under Taranagar tehsil. The accused, identified as Ramchandra Jat, has been taken into custody, and an investigation is underway. The incident comes ahead of the panchayat elections inTaranagar, where voting for the posts of panch and sarpanch is scheduled for November 16.

Article Title: Nana Patekar or Smit Machchhar? Mumbai's new East-West Vidyavihar bridge gets caught in naming row
Article Text:
Row over Mumbai's Vidyavihar bridge name

Vidyavihar bridge in Mumbai: Key features





MUMBAI: A naming row has erupted over Mumbai's newly constructed East-West Vidyavihar bridge ahead of its opening to traffic, with Shiv Sena (UBT) demanding that the structure be named after actor Nana Patekar , while BJP MLA Parag Shah has proposed naming it after Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian commercial pilot hailed for thwarting a mid-air hijacking.The Shiv Sena (UBT) recently put up a banner on the bridge demanding that it be named 'Padma Shri Nana Patekar Setu', days after Shah approached the authorities with a request to name it after Captain Machchhar.Machchhar was hailed globally as a hero after thwarting a violent mid-air hijacking of a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight.Earlier this week, a delegation of Sena (UBT) leaders met Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde and submitted a letter demanding that the bridge be named after Patekar.Tawde could not be reached for comment despite repeated attempts. However, Ganesh Khankar, leader of the house in the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), accused Sena (UBT) of stoking a controversy to claim credit for the naming proposal."Nana Patekar was one of the most talented actors in the country. I feel that it would be more fitting to name a large theatre or a theatre complex after him rather than a bridge," Khankar said.The much-delayed, 650-metre-long, two-lane East-West Vidyavihar bridge connects Ramchandra Chemburkar Marg on the eastern side of Vidyavihar railway station with Lal Bahadur Shastri Marg on the western side in Ghatkopar.According to the BMC, the bridge has a 100-metre section passing over railway tracks. Its approach roads measure 220 metres on the eastern side and 330 metres on the western side.The project also includes access links connecting the bridge to the station's footpaths, along with the reconstruction of ticket booking offices, the station master's office and staircases, the civic body said.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Mumbai's newly constructed East-West Vidyavihar bridge has sparked a naming row. Shiv Sena demands that the structure be named after actor Nana Patekar. BJP MLA Parag Shah has proposed naming it after Captain Smit Machchhar.Machchhar was hailed globally after thwarting a violent mid-air hijacking.

Article Title: ‘1838 is about representing and recognising the history of both The Times and of India’
Article Text:
Satyan Gajwani, Vice Chairman, Times Internet Ltd, speaking at the launch of 1838 Reserve credit card

The 1838 Reserve ICICI Bank credit card

Kumar Mangalam Birla with Samir Jain, Vice Chairman, BCCL

A NAME THAT CARRIES 188 YEARS OF HISTORY

When we think about the future, it’s about commemorating the leaders that will take this generation and this country to its next level. And that’s what this card is really meant for.

this is really his, more than anyone else’s

(L-R) Dr Pradeep Chowbey, Amit Khanna and Raj Thota

Avarna Jain

Sandeep Batra and Rakesh Jha

Aman Nath

we thought what’s the best partner to do that with. No guesses, it’s going to be ICICI Bank and The Times of India,”

Mandira Wirk

Chef Garima Arora

CRIMSON BLOOMS AND A CANDLELIGHT DINNER

Performance by Roysten Abel's Manganiyar Seduction

An ode to 188 years: 1838 Reserve credit card





Crimson floral decor, gold accents and a backdrop of grand architectural facades set the scene. For guests, however, a rare delight awaited in an exhibition of veteran artist Krishen Khanna’s iconic Bandwalla series. The maestro himself graced the evening and interacted with guests. As 1,838 parrots took to the skies, the celebrations extended beyond the crimson setting and art, music and culinary experiences came together in Delhi on Monday evening at the launch of 1838 Reserve ICICI Bank credit card by The Times of India , in association with ICICI Bank and Visa.Hosted by Samir Jain , Vice Chairman, BCCL, and Satyan Gajwani, Vice Chairman, Times Internet Ltd, the evening celebrated the card’s launch and 188 years of The Times of India, which first went to print in 1838. In addition to the eminent guests from the banking and corporate sectors, prominent guests present at the event included Karisma Kapoor, Aman Nath, Avarna Jain, Sunil Sethi, Mandira Wirk and Rina Dhaka.The gathering at the family home gave the occasion a personal touch, which reflected in Satyan’s welcome address too. “When we think about the name of the card, 1838 Reserve, it stands for the beginning of The Times of India and the 188 years of legacy and history where we’ve chronicled and followed and watched India change.The story of India is made by its creators, its builders, its leaders, its artists. This card is about commemorating them and commemorating their work.1838 really is about representing and recognising the history of both The Times and of India, and it’s about thinking about what the future looks like. For us, bridging the past and the future is really what feels so special, and we believe this card is going to play a major role in doing that.” Speaking about the partnerships, Satyan continued, “This card is not built by us alone. We’ve had amazing partners along the way. ICICI Bank took a big punt with us a few years ago in launching the Times Black card. Fortunately, it’s been incredibly successful, one of the best-performing new cards. It was always the starting point, and we wanted to do something more. While that card is a great opportunity, this card holds a very special place for us because it really is like taking a piece of our history and making it something people can carry around with them. Visa has also been an incredible partner, and someday someone will tell you the story where we were this close to not working with Visa. I also want to thank my father-in-law, Samir Jain, for letting us use not just his home, but his legacy, because.”Khanna’s Bandwalla artwork finds a new home on the card, while the exhibition at the event offered guests a closer look at the series. Its brass-band musicians, familiar figures in Indian wedding processions, have occupied a central place in his artistic universe for more than 50 years. Talking about Khanna’s artwork on the card, Satyan said, “Art plays a very important part in our family’s lives. My wife (Trishla Jain) is an artist and our home is adorned with beautiful art. So, when we had the opportunity to work with sir Krishen Khanna, it was an opportunity none of us felt we could miss. We’re so grateful that the person who has chronicled the ordinary lives of Indians for decades, and whose figures of the bandwallahs are as iconic as the country itself, is with us here. While we’ve all seen his works on walls, to be able to carry it in your pocket is something special for us.” For guests, the opportunity to meet the artist brought forth memorable moments. Sunil Sethi, Chairman, Fashion Design Council of India (FDCI), said, “I have always been a huge fan of his (Khanna’s) works and to meet him here was special. He knew my father-in-law, and when I went to meet him, it was so surprising that he recognised me and gave me his blessings.”Rakesh Jha, Executive Director, ICICI Bank, said, “All the hard work of The Times of India team, team ICICI, and VISA, has come to fruition today with the launch of this new card. For us, what matters is how we earn and retain the trust of the customer. And at all points of time, we believe in our core philosophy of being fair to the customer and fair to the bank.A credit card is an important part of our overall product portfolio. This card is indeed most special.”“When Visa thought about launching for the first time the Visa Infinite Privilege tier in India,said Rishi Chhabra, Country Manager, Visa India, about the partnership and added, “So what’s Visa Infinite Privilege tier all about? We’ve had the Visa Infinite for years, in fact, decades, where we know and respect that extraordinary folks need something extraordinary every day. And that’s when Visa Infinite Privilege stepped in. With the global experiences, unparalleled access, stronger recognition, the best service to go with it, we thought of launching this tier globally, in Asia-Pacific, and in India. So proud of doing this with our partners.”The evening’s culinary offerings began with fusion Indian dishes created by chef Manish Mehrotra and his team. Later, guests gathered for a dinner curated by Michelin-starred chef Garima Arora, with crimson florals and candlelight carrying the evening’s colour palette to the tables. “From the magnificent art of Krishen Khanna ji to the almost divine music of the Manganiyars, every moment was an experience to cherish. The dinner setting, adorned with beautiful red roses and candlelight, was breathtaking, and the exquisite food by chef Garima was simply delicious. Art, music, heritage and gastronomy came together so beautifully, making it an evening that celebrated culture, creativity and meaningful conversations,” said designer Mandira Wirk, summing up the evening’s experience.
Article Summary: 1838 Reserve credit card launched by The Times of India and ICICI Bank. Krishen Khanna’s iconic Bandwalla series found a home on the card. 1,838 parrots took to the skies to celebrate the card's launch.

Article Title: ​Injured European Roller treated & rescued
Article Text:
Injured European roller offered feed

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





An injured European Roller, a rare migratory bird, was rescued and treated before being released back into the wild recently.Private school teachers Bhaskar Shinde and Sanjay Tayde spotted the bird lying injured on the school premises in Satara and alerted conservationist Kishor Pathak.Pathak dispatched rescuers Akash Waghmare and Datta Baravkar to the spot, who safely secured the bird. “A medical examination revealed an injury to the bird’s left wing, possibly sustained while hunting prey. The wound was cleaned and treated. The bird was kept under observation and provided with its natural diet. After making a full recovery, the European roller was released into the wild,” Pathak said.European Roller breeds across Central Asia and Europe. During winter snowfall, it migrates to India and onwards to Africa. In recent years, the species, which resembles Indian roller, has regularly been sighted in the region during winter.“The bird is found in hilly areas, grasslands, scrublands and farmlands with low trees and bushes. It perches on bush tips and electric wires and hunts insects, scorpions, rodents and caterpillars from the ground. Considered a farmer’s friend, it is also called Dev Pakshi for its ecological importance,” Pathak said.
Article Summary: A rare migratory bird was rescued and treated before being released back into the wild. Private school teachers Bhaskar Shinde and Sanjay Tayde spotted the bird lying injured on the school premises in Satara and alerted conservationist Kishor Pathak. The bird was kept under observation and provided with its natural diet.

Article Title: Hingoli man kills wife at in-laws’ farm, attacks mother-in-law; later ends life
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A dispute over a woman staying at her parental home ended in a double tragedy in Hingoli district on Wednesday evening. A man allegedly bludgeoned his wife to death, seriously injured his mother-in-law when she tried to intervene, and later died by suicide by hanging himself from a nearby tree.The deceased were identified as Deepali Paikrao and her husband Vishal Dongre, both in their mid-20s. Deepali’s mother, Kamalbai, sustained serious injuries and is undergoing treatment.According to police, both families are engaged in farming.Hingoli superintendent of police Shrenik Lodha said, “Deepali had married Vishal, a resident of Dhanora Jahangir village. However, she had returned to her parental home, in Kharwad village of Kalamnuri taluka, after Vishal allegedly began harassing her following their marriage.”She had been staying with her parents at their agricultural field for the past few days. Police said Vishal had repeatedly asked Deepali to return with him. On Wednesday evening, he went to her parents’ farm to convince her to come back. An argument broke out between the couple over her decision to stay with her parents.In a fit of rage, Vishal allegedly picked up a wooden plank from a cot and struck Deepali on the head. She died on the spot.When Kamalbai rushed to stop the assault, Vishal allegedly attacked her as well, leaving her severely injured.Some time later, Kamalbai’s husband and son arrived at the farm, found the victims and took them to hospital. They then alerted the police.During the subsequent search, police found Vishal hanging from a tree a few metres away from the scene of the crime.Based on Kamalbai’s complaint, Kalamnuri police on Thursday registered a murder case against Vishal. Senior officers visited the spot and carried out a panchanama.

When interrogated, the tractor driver was unable to give any justification or provide documents,” said assistant conservator of forests Jayashree Jadhav.The tractor driver, Gorakh Shiratode, has been taken into custody. “The seized goods have been safely kept at Varade forest department office for security reasons,” Jadhav added.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.

Article Title: Three held for tying up, robbing 60-year-old woman of jewellery worth Rs 58.87 lakh
Article Text:
Deputy commissioner of police Shewta Khedkar said robbers were arrested with help of CCTV footage

Pune:





Chikhali police on Friday arrested three men for allegedly tying up a 60-year-old woman at her bungalow and robbing her of gold and silver jewellery and cash collectively worth Rs 58.87 lakh on Oct 13. The police have recovered the entire booty from the accused.A police team led by senior police inspector Ranjeet Jadhav arrested the accused — Anarulla Chaudhari (36) of Kudalwadi, Abdul Momin (39) of Kandivali in Mumbai and Samiullah Khan (32) of Mumbra — with the help of CCTV footage and a tip-off.Jadhav told TOI that Chaudhari had been thrown out of his house and needed money to fund his addictions. The other two accused were his childhood friends. He contacted them and hatched a plan to commit a theft at a godown in Kudalwadi. The duo came to Chikhali on Oct 12.The three were having tea at an eatery near the victim’s house in Jyotibanagar, Talawade. “They learnt that the eatery owner lived in a nearby bungalow. When they walked past the bungalow, they found that it was the only one in the area, surrounded by shops,” Jadhav said.He said the accused saw an elderly woman going to the first floor of the bungalow, while the door to the ground floor was locked.“The trio then hatched a plan to rob the woman,” he said.Around 1.30am on Oct 13, the trio allegedly broke the locks of the main door and barged into the woman’s first-floor residence. One of them sat on the woman while she was fast asleep, and his accomplices tied her limbs and gagged her with a sari. They allegedly assaulted her and threatened her with a knife before fleeing with 730gm of gold jewellery and silver jewellery collectively worth Rs 57.87 lakh.“After receiving the complaint, our team swung into action. We checked more than 70 CCTV cameras and traced the accused’s motorcycle. We could not trace the motorcycle beyond Kudalwadi, following which we focused our investigation there,” Jadhav said.He added that the police acted on a tip-off received by inspector Amol Phadtare and took the trio into custody. The police also seized the motorcycle and a sharp weapon from them.
Article Summary: Three men arrested for allegedly tying up a 60-year-old woman at her bungalow and robbing her of gold and silver jewellery and cash collectively worth Rs 58.87 lakh. The police have recovered the entire booty from the accused.

Article Title: Vidya Valley School shines at World Youth Forum 2026
Article Text:
Vidya Valley School Shines at World Youth Forum 2026

Pune:





Vidya Valley School participated in the Liberal Arts & Leadership Summit organised by World Youth Forum 2026, held in Macau, China, providing its students with an enriching opportunity to learn, compete and collaborate with young minds from across the globe.The journey began months before the Forum, with students, teachers, coaches and parents working together with dedication and enthusiasm. Students researched the global issue of climate change, developed presentations, strengthened their communication skills and learned the value of teamwork. The preparation itself became a meaningful extension of classroom learning.The Vidya Valley delegation comprised Aneya Patwardhan, Agastya Sharan, Kabir Dhole, Ayaan Kulkarni, Jian Humane, Kiaan Kamat, Rukmini Karandikar, Paarmita Khandare, Shaurya Mehta, Rugved Bhujbal, Arya Kadam, Aryaa Jathar, Rhea Thattil and Zubin Vahanvati, accompanied by Jayashree Ghorpade and Rachana Nautiyal.At the Forum, Vidya Valley students participated in a wide range of academic, creative, presentation and leadership events. Interacting with participants from diverse countries and cultures, they demonstrated confidence, curiosity, resilience and the ability to express their ideas on an international platform.The team returned with an extraordinary 74 awards, including 53 medals, including 19 gold, 15 silver and 14 bronze, bringing immense pride to the entire Vidya Valley community.Ipsita Rodricks, Director, Vidya Valley School, said, “The true achievement goes far beyond the medals. The experience encouraged students to listen to different perspectives, respect diverse cultures, work under pressure and discover their own potential. They learnt that success is not merely about winning, but about challenging oneself, learning from others and growing through every experience.”For the teachers and mentors, witnessing students grow into confident young global citizens was the most rewarding outcome. The Forum beautifully reflected Vidya Valley School’s philosophy of holistic education—preparing children not merely for examinations, but for life and for the larger world.The World Youth Forum 2026 will remain a cherished chapter in the school’s journey, celebrating curiosity, collaboration, courage and lifelong learning—a remarkable journey from the classroom to the world stage.
Article Summary: Vidya Valley School participated in the Liberal Arts & Leadership Summit organised by World Youth Forum 2026, held in Macau, China. The team returned with an extraordinary 74 awards, including 53 medals, including 19 gold, 15 silver and 14 bronze.
